summary: Security misconfigurations and suspicious activity detected.

findings.title: Container Running as Root
evidence: No USER instruction is present in the Dockerfile
findings.description: The Dockerfile never switches to a non-root user, so the application process runs as root by default inside the container.
findings.recommendation: Create a dedicated non-root user and switch to it with a USER instruction.

findings.title: Unnecessary SSH Service
findings.description: Unnecessary SSH components increase attack surface.

findings.title: Hardcoded Credential
findings.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials and use runtime secrets.

findings.title: Debug Mode Enabled
findings.description: Debug settings may expose sensitive information.

attack_analysis: Three suspicious events originated from source IP 198.51.100.45. The sequence started with PORT_SCAN targeting port 22, followed by a failed AUTH_ATTEMPT against root, and an EXPLOITATION_ATTEMPT targeting the debug endpoint on port 5000. The SSH-related events may be relevant to the Dockerfile installing openssh-server and declaring EXPOSE 22. The debug endpoint attempt may be relevant to DEBUG_MODE=true and the hardcoded credential-like value. These events indicate suspicious activity, but there is no evidence of successful compromise.
patch:
FROM python:3.11-slim
RUN groupadd -r appuser && useradd -r -g appuser appuser
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY --chown=appuser:appuser . .
USER appuser
EXPOSE 5000
CMD ["python", "app.py"]
containment_actions: Recommend investigating and temporarily blocking the suspicious IP in an isolated test environment.
tests: Verify the container runs as non-root.
